subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add a core lifecycle event contract for sub-agent `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` states, or solve startup silence through existing lifecycle/status fields instead?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the requested fix adds new core event semantics across agent, gateway, session, and SDK consumers, and the open PR candidate is stale against renamed runtime files.

options.title: Add explicit lifecycle phases
options.body: Sponsor a current-main implementation of `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` through the active embedded-agent, subagent, gateway, session, SDK, docs, and tests surfaces.

options.title: Reuse existing lifecycle fields
options.body: Reject new phases and require a narrower fix that uses current `start`/`end`/`error` plus terminal metadata to distinguish startup failure and first progress.

options.title: Defer until live corpus proof
options.body: Keep the issue open but wait for reporter-provided transcript fixtures or a maintained repro harness before accepting any event-contract change.

recommendation.title: Add explicit lifecycle phases
recommendation.body: Sponsor a current-main implementation of `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` through the active embedded-agent, subagent, gateway, session, SDK, docs, and tests surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent git history shows steipete carrying the active lifecycle/runtime rename and subagent registry surfaces that any current-main implementation must touch.
